Hearth & Empire · a 3D strategy game of rival nations

A throne stands empty.

Thirteen nations need a ruler. Give one your name, your judgement and your voice, then meet yourself in the campaign.

Choose your nation

Stop after any step, press Download, and send that one file back to whoever invited you. Nothing is uploaded anywhere: your work stays in this browser tab until you download it, and is lost if you close the tab first.

Already started? Open the file you downloaded last time and carry on, for example to add your voice.

I

Who they are

Make this character your own

The leader below is only a starting point. Rename them, change their title, give them a portrait, and rewrite any of their lines; in the campaign they will appear and speak as you made them. Leave anything as it is to keep it.

Their portrait (optional; shown in a circle beside their words. Pick one of these for now, or use a picture of your own.)

Portraits and the paintings behind this page are public-domain works from The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Open Access.

II

How they rule

How do they rule?

Answer as your leader would. When you are not the one playing this nation, the computer plays it the way you answer: how readily it goes to war, whether its towns turn to the church or the tavern, whether it walls itself in or rides out, and how it bargains. Skip any question, or all of them, to leave the nation as it was written.

You can stop here. Steps 1 and 2 are enough for your leader to appear in the campaign as you made them, with their lines shown as text. Download and send the file now, and come back to add your voice whenever you like: open this page again and choose Continue from a saved file.

III

Their words and voiceOptional. Do it now, later, or not at all.

How they were written (play them your own way if you prefer):


Tips: a quiet room, the microphone a hand's width from your mouth, and leave half a second of silence before you speak. Each line should run two to six seconds. Record as many or as few as you like; unrecorded lines stay as text in the game. Each box says when the leader speaks the line: keep your own version to that moment, and to one or two sentences.
